symptoms: The skin of the potato tuber develops rough, corky spots.
You may see superficial reddish-brown spots on the surface of young tubers.
As the potato grows, these spots expand and become pitted or cracked.
Severe cases leave the potato skin covered in rough black welts.
The damaged areas may attract insects.
favourable_conditions: The disease is common in fields with low soil pH and is made worse by high soil moisture or too much irrigation.
prevention: Only plant seed potatoes that are free from scab.
Use a crop rotation of four to six years with alfalfa.
Add green manure to your fields before planting potatoes.
Avoid using alkaline fertilizers like calcium ammonium nitrate.
practices: Remove any damaged or rotten potatoes before placing the crop in storage.
If you wash the tubers, allow them to dry thoroughly before storing.
Keep potatoes in a dark, well-ventilated cool place for 10 to 14 days after harvest to allow cuts and bruises to heal.
